text:
Aisha: Quick thread — need a sharp one-pager vs big cloud vendors for next week's webinar. Target: succinct rebut lines + 2x data points, routing guidance for inbound leads.
Ryan: Got it. I'll pull perf and cost numbers. Which claims do we want to push first: latency, cost, or deployment flexibility?
Aisha: Prioritize predictable latency at scale, predictable cost (reserved/dedicated), and hybrid/private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Avoid absolute % claims unless we link to the raw benchmark.
Lena: We have a 30d p99 stat: `p99 = 120ms` for seq=512 on our dedicated pool. Want that surfaced?
Tom: Yes but frame it as consistency: "consistent p99 under predictable load". Also call out autoscaling + burst capacity + fallback routing to quantized variants.
Ryan: Draft bullets I'm thinking: 1) Predictable p99 latency under reserved capacity; 2) Lower unit economics through batching + caching; 3) Runs in customer VPCs or on-prem — same API. Keep short.
Maya: For direct rebut vs CloudX where they push "freshness": argue application SLAs beat raw model freshness. Snappy line: "Model access is not the same as application-level SLAs."
Lena: Where should the one-pager live? marketing repo or webinar assets?
Aisha: Put the first draft in /marketing/webinar-assets and ping the webinar script team when ready. @ops-bot can you validate the infra numbers quickly?
ops-bot: Running validation query: `SELECT p99 FROM infra.metrics WHERE stack='dedicated' AND seq_len=512 AND period='30d'`. Result: p99=120ms, median=118ms. Dashboard updated in #eng-metrics.
Ryan: Good — I'll avoid an absolute "% cheaper" claim. Use unit-econ wording: "reduces per-token cost via smart batching and prefix caching" and include a footnote link to the cost model.
Tom: :thumbsup: Also add a one-liner on graceful degradation: automatic fallback to quantized model variants and cross-region failover.
Aisha: Plan: draft by EOD tomorrow, hand to webinar script team Friday. Volunteers to polish copy?
Maya: I can do copy polish Friday morning.
Ryan: Draft link (when ready) will be here: https://git.redwood/marketing/webinar/sniper-sprint-draft.md
Aisha: Perfect — quick asks: Lena, please add exact source links next to each quantitative claim; Tom, add a short ops note on rollout safety and canary thresholds. We'll iterate in the doc. Thanks!
